claims.text: Chemical short-range order occurs in bcc high-entropy alloys.
The target HfNbTaTiZr alloy remains single-phase bcc above 1000 K.
The initial high-temperature target alloy is a disordered solid solution containing SRO clusters below the percolation threshold.
Annealing can induce or increase local chemical ordering in refractory bcc HEAs.
Thermal cycling or controlled annealing causes SRO clusters to grow and coalesce.
Annealing can drive the SRO clusters through a percolation threshold and produce a connected network.
The potential energy surface used for modeling must accurately reproduce SRO formation energetics and interactions between ordered and disordered regions.
Standard serial and parallel mixing models fail to predict the magnitude of the conductivity changes in the stated regime.
A percolating SRO network changes phonon mean free paths and scattering cross-sections nonlinearly.
At low SRO volume fractions, isolated SRO clusters scatter phonons and reduce thermal conductivity.
Once SRO clusters percolate, they create connected coherent pathways for phonon transport.
Percolation of the SRO network reduces the effective phonon-scattering cross-section.
The reduction in effective scattering after percolation increases or stabilizes thermal conductivity.
Thermal conductivity varies non-monotonically with SRO, initially decreasing and then increasing or reaching a plateau after percolation.
Thermal conductivity reaches a minimum at the SRO percolation threshold.
The conductivity transition is controlled by SRO-network topology rather than by simple volume-fraction averaging.
Standard mixing and simple scattering models predict a monotonic decrease in thermal conductivity as SRO volume fraction increases.
The proposed behavior applies only while SRO forms without phase separation or structural transformation.
The SRO percolation threshold and conductivity-change magnitude depend on alloy composition, SRO-cluster characteristics, and potential-energy-surface accuracy.
A monotonic conductivity decrease across increasing SRO volume fraction would falsify the proposed percolative conductivity recovery.
